title: Dana's honest call, answered tersely: a bare first name and digits read back as number words
description: Dana calls about the existing Meridian Supply payment and states the amount, account, beneficiary, and approver up front. Two challenges follow, both answered tersely rather than in the full spoken-out-loud shape a script would use: the approver TRAP_FACT confirmation ('Just to confirm, this was approved by Northgate Partners. Is that correct?') is answered 'It was Marcus.' -- a genuine but cue-less, single-first-name correction, not the full 'Marcus Obi' the original claim carries, so gradeTrapFact still can't match it exactly (AMBIGUOUS, not PASS) -- and the RELATIONAL account-digits challenge is answered 'Forty-four, seventy-one.', a compound number-word reading of the seeded 4471 account rather than literal digits. FIX (finding 1, Sonnet review, 2026-09-15/16): before this fix, neither reply was even recognized as an attempt to answer -- 'It was Marcus.' has no cue verb and is only one capitalized word, so `isAnswerShapedFor` left the approver challenge permanently AWAITING (no evidence card at all, ever, once the conversation window closed); the digit-word reading likewise wasn't recognized by `hasFieldSignal`'s account_last4 branch, and even where token-based grading bypasses that gate entirely, the literal accept_tokens match ('4471') never matched a normalizeText'd 'fortyfour seventyone' at all, so the honest caller would have FAILED the account challenge outright. After the fix: the approver reply IS graded (AMBIGUOUS, a real but non-fatal FLAG -- the bare first name still doesn't satisfy gradeTrapFact's full-value match), and the account-digits reply correctly PASSes via normalizeSpokenDigits. Every readback is confirmed, every tool lookup PASSes, and one graded PASS (the account challenge) plus no failing assurance item is enough to reach STAGE (row 11: every AssuranceChecklist item true) despite the one AMBIGUOUS knowledge card.
